assistant|meeting_duration_recommendatio: Assistant recommended keeping team meetings to about 60-90 minutes to maintain attention and engagement
assistant|conflict_resolution_tips: Assistant advised staying calm, focusing on issues not people, using 'I' statements, seeking common ground, and being open to compromise
assistant|team_meeting_prep: Assistant suggested preparing an agenda, encouraging open communication, taking notes, and following up with a summary after the meeting
assistant|task_prioritization_strategies: Assistant suggested identifying most important topics first, categorizing by urgency and impact, and aligning topics with team goals
assistant|time_allocation_strategies: Assistant suggested assigning time blocks, using a parking lot, leaving 5-10 minute buffers between topics, and allowing time for questions
assistant|agenda_template_example: Assistant provided a sample agenda table with columns for Topic, Priority, Time Allocation, and Objective (e.g., 15 min project update, 30 min feature discussion, 10 min feedback)
assistant|in_meeting_time_management: Assistant suggested starting on time, using a timer, encouraging brevity, intervening when off track, and periodically summarizing
assistant|off_agenda_handling_strategies: Assistant suggested acknowledging/validating the concern, evaluating urgency, then parking lot, separate discussion, brief update, or delegating to a smaller group
assistant|note_taking_during_meeting: Assistant suggested choosing a note-taking method, capturing decisions/action items/questions, using a template, abbreviations like AI/DEC/Q, and clarifying unclear points
assistant|post_meeting_note_organization: Assistant suggested reviewing/organizing notes, identifying action items and owners, creating summary/minutes, sharing with the team, and storing centrally
assistant|digital_note_tools: Assistant recommended note-taking apps (Evernote, OneNote, Simplenote), collaborative tools (Google Docs, Microsoft Teams, Trello), and meeting tools (MeetingSphere, MeetingKing, MinuteDock)
assistant|note_taking_best_practices: Assistant recommended being consistent, reviewing/updating notes regularly, using clear concise language, and including context like dates and attendees
assistant|note_template_formats: Assistant described basic, structured, and mind map templates plus Cornell Notes, outline, and table formats for meeting notes
assistant|digital_template_examples: Assistant listed OneNote templates (meeting notes, project meeting, brainstorming), Evernote templates (meeting notes, project management, task list), and Google Docs templates (meeting minutes, project plan, notes)
assistant|additional_digital_tools: Assistant mentioned Trello (visual project management), Simplenote (minimalist note-taking), and Bear (note-taking with focus mode) as additional tools
